answer_1.quote: We experiment on machine translation (MT), text summarization (SUM), and data-to-text (D2T), and show that BARTScore++ consistently and significantly improves the performance of vanilla BARTScore, and surpasses existing top-scoring metrics in 19 out of 25 test settings...
answer_1.outputs: generated text in machine translation, summarization, and data-to-text tasks

answer_2.quote: We compare our method with several commonly used baseline metrics for evaluating text generation, including BLEU, BERTScore, MoverScore and PRISM. For MT tasks, we also consider supervised metrics that leverage human judgments to train, including COMET and BLEURT.

answer_3.quote: Besides taking BARTScore as the testbed to verify the effectiveness of our proposed error-analysis evaluation strategy, we also show the universality in the recently advanced language model ChatGPT by designing an error-analysis-based prompt.

answer_4.quote: We also consider Multidimensional Quality Metric (MQM) for zh-en provided by  in §6, comprising judgments of 8 best-performing translation systems in WMT20, annotated by professional translators.
answer_4.guideline: MQM requires evaluators to identify errors and categorize them into different levels according to their severity. For instance, mistranslations and hallucinations are mostly considered as Major errors, and imperfections in fluency are often marked as Minor errors.
